text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Inspection reveals an erythematous plaque with areas of crusting, oozing, and irregular borders observed on the dorsal surface of the penile shaft and on the left middle finger. Palpation shows lesions are firm to touch, non-tender, with no warmth. Regional lymph nodes (cervical, axillary, inguinal) are not palpable. Biopsy findings indicate cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium. STD panel (Syphilis, HIV, HBV, HCV) is negative.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma (cutaneous) with distant spread to the penile shaft and finger.

The biopsy showing nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures confirms malignancy, and the presence of identical lesions on unrelated sites (penis and finger) strongly suggests metastatic disease rather than a primary infection or benign condition.
